 Indonesia should compensate Malaysians for the prolonged haze – Guan Eng
 Alternatively, it should agree to establish a permanent transboundary haze relief task force that can aid its counterparts in Indonesia to douse the embers of haze there, said Lim.
 Updated 3 hours ago · Published on 18 Nov 2026 9:59AM
 Prabowo also cannot reject responsibility for how long it went on, exacerbated as it is by the Super El Nino this year. - November 18, 2026 
 by Ian McIntyre
 FORMER Finance Minister Lim Guan Eng has called for Indonesia to compensate Malaysia for its welfare and economic losses of some RM13 billion due to the prolonged haze.
 Alternatively, it should agree to establish a permanent transboundary haze relief task force to help its counterparts in Indonesia douse the embers of haze there, Lim said.
 In the interests of good neighbourly relations and the ASEAN spirit of solidarity, he said, Malaysia should accept an apology from Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to Malaysia and Singapore over this year's extended haze crisis.
 Prabowo also cannot reject responsibility for how long it went on, exacerbated as it is by the Super El Nino this year.
 In a study commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers for the period July 1until  October 22, 2026, economists warned that severe air pollution reduces international tourist arrivals by up to eight per cent, threatening the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign and risking up to RM5 billion in broader tourism-related gross domestic product or spillovers.
 What is of concern is that the health - related welfare losses of RM 8 billion reflect society's economic valuation of avoiding premature mortality risk—linked to an estimated 1,700 premature deaths.
 This is 1,700 senior Malaysian citizens dying prematurely.
 For this reason, air purifiers become essential haze prevention devices, said Lim.
 "I had suggested a RM 1,000 tax rebate for those who purchased air purifiers during this critical period to look after our young and senior citizens."
 If Indonesia cannot afford to pay, then they should be magnanimous and humane by agreeing to establish the proposed transboundary haze relief task force that can immediately operate and conduct fire-fighting efforts in Indonesian forests, said Lim.
 Indonesia had rejected this permanent task force comprising trained fire-fighters to enter Indonesian forests immediately on grounds of guarding its national sovereignty.
 Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan should convey this proposal to Indonesia on behalf of 34 million Malaysians that haze should not be permitted to be an annual recurring event.
 Only a permanent fire-fighting task force comprising trained personnel, with the authority to enter Indonesian forests immediately once a fire is detected, can ASEAN prevent haze from becoming an annual disaster, he added. - November 18, 2026.
